title: Assignment 24 · Limitations on damages
summary: Limitations on damages. Assigned readings and principal cases for this class.
notes:
Rockingham County v. Luten Bridge Co.: After receiving the county’s repudiation, a bridge builder could recover its legitimate breach losses but could not enlarge recovery by continuing to build a bridge the county no longer wanted.

Parker v. Twentieth Century-Fox Film Corp.: An actress did not have to accept a different and inferior substitute role to reduce damages after the studio cancelled her promised musical role.

Hadley v. Baxendale: A carrier was not liable for the mill’s lost profits on the facts the court accepted because the exceptional consequences of delay had not been sufficiently communicated when the shipping contract was made.

Kenford Co. v. County of Erie: The county’s knowledge that a stadium would increase surrounding land values did not establish that it assumed liability for Kenford’s lost appreciation if the stadium was never built.

Fera v. Village Plaza, Inc.: A new business could recover projected profits when detailed evidence supported a reasonable estimate; lack of an operating history was not an automatic bar.
